value.name: Olympiacos beat AEK Athens on penalties after a 4-4 draw in the Greek Cup final
value.hint: The shootout finished 15-14 after eight goals in normal and extra time, with Matt Derbyshire scoring twice for Olympiacos.

archive.notes: Date, 4-4 after extra time and 15-14 shootout agree in Wikipedia and UEFA; scorer names agree.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Atromitos 2-1 after extra time in the Greek Cup final
value.hint: Played at the Olympic Stadium in Athens; Olympiacos won the cup under Ernesto Valverde.

archive.notes: Date, score, extra time and venue agree. Wikipedia lists only Djebbour for Olympiacos, UEFA also names Fuster, so scorers omitted.

value.name: Olympiacos beat AEK Athens 1-0 in the Greek Cup final at Volos
value.hint: Lazar Randelovic scored in the ninth minute in a stadium closed to the public.

archive.notes: Date, score, scorer, minute and venue agree.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Aris 2-0 in the Greek Cup final in Thessaloniki

value.name: Olympiacos beat Asteras Tripolis 3-1 after extra time in the Greek Cup final
value.hint: Played at the Olympic Stadium in Athens.

archive.notes: Date, score, extra time and venue agree; scorer lists differ between sources so omitted.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Panathinaikos 2-0 in the Greek Cup final
value.hint: Dimitris Mavrogenidis scored in the 54th minute and the win completed a domestic double.

archive.notes: Date, score and Mavrogenidis 54th minute agree; second scorer is Ofori-Quaye (90th vs 89th minute, minute omitted). Double is stated in Wikipedia.

value.name: Olympiacos beat AEK Athens 3-0 in the Greek Cup final in Heraklion

value.name: Olympiacos beat Aris 3-0 in the Greek Cup final in Patras

archive.notes: Date, score and Patras venue agree.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Xanthi 3-1 in the Greek Cup final to complete a domestic double

value.name: Olympiacos beat OFI 2-0 in the Greek Cup final

archive.notes: Date, score, title number and gap agree.

value.name: Olympiacos beat AEK Athens 1-0 at home to clinch the league title
value.hint: The title was secured in the third round of the championship play-offs.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Manchester United 2-0 in the Champions League round of 16 first leg
value.hint: Alejandro Dominguez scored in the 38th minute at Karaiskakis Stadium.

archive.notes: Date, score, venue and the 38th-minute goal agree; the second scorer Joel Campbell is named by both, his minute differs (50th vs 55th) so omitted.

value.name: Manchester United won 3-0 at home to knock Olympiacos out of the Champions League
value.hint: Robin van Persie scored a hat-trick and United went through 3-2 on aggregate.

archive.notes: Date, score, aggregate and hat-trick agree.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Juventus 1-0 in a Champions League group match
value.hint: Pajtim Kasami scored in the 36th minute at Karaiskakis Stadium.

archive.notes: Date, score, venue and scorer agree; another outlet gave the following day, which is its publication day.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Arsenal 3-1 in the final Champions League group match but missed out on the last 16
value.hint: Results elsewhere in the group sent the club into the Europa League.

archive.notes: Date, score, scorers and outcome agree; David Fuster minute differs (36th vs 45th) so omitted.

value.name: Arsenal won 1-0 in Piraeus in the Europa League round of 32 first leg
value.hint: Alexandre Lacazette scored in the 81st minute.

archive.notes: Date, score and scorer agree across three publishers.

value.name: Olympiacos won 2-1 after extra time at Arsenal to go through on away goals
value.hint: Youssef El Arabi scored in the final seconds of extra time at the Emirates Stadium.

archive.notes: TNT Sports, Wikipedia and Guernsey Press (URL dated 2020/02/27) agree on 27 February, the 2-1 extra-time result and the El Arabi goal. A fourth outlet (90min) gave a different day, which is consistent with a next-day publication date and is not cited.

value.name: Olympiacos drew 1-1 with Wolverhampton Wanderers in the Europa League round of 16 first leg
value.hint: Played at Karaiskakis Stadium.

archive.notes: Date, score and venue agree. Neos Kosmos dates it the next day (publication day) and is not cited.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Ferencvaros 1-0 in the Conference League knockout play-off first leg
value.hint: Played at Karaiskakis Stadium in Piraeus.

archive.notes: Date, score and round agree.

value.name: Olympiacos won 1-0 at Ferencvaros to take the Conference League play-off 2-0 on aggregate
value.hint: Played in Budapest.

archive.notes: Date, score and round agree.

value.name: Olympiacos lost 4-1 at home to Maccabi Tel Aviv in the Conference League round of 16 first leg
value.hint: Played at Karaiskakis Stadium in Piraeus.

archive.notes: Date (7 March in UEFA; Neos Kosmos report published next morning in Australia), score and venue agree.

value.name: Olympiacos won 6-1 after extra time at Maccabi Tel Aviv to turn round the Conference League tie
value.hint: The tie finished 7-5 on aggregate; the match was played at a venue in Backa Topola, Serbia.

archive.notes: Date, score, venue and all six goals with minutes agree between FotMob and Football Web Pages; UEFA confirms the 6-1 win.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Fenerbahce 3-2 at home in the Conference League quarter-final first leg
value.hint: Played at Karaiskakis Stadium; Fortounis, Jovetic and Chiquinho scored.

archive.notes: Date, score and scorer names agree; scorer minutes differ between reports so omitted.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Fenerbahce 3-2 on penalties after losing 1-0 in extra time in Istanbul
value.hint: The tie finished 3-3 on aggregate and Olympiacos reached the semi-final.

archive.notes: Date, score, extra time and shootout result agree between FotMob and UEFA. A Daily Sabah preview gives the day before and is not cited.

value.name: Olympiacos lost 4-3 at home to Real Madrid in a Champions League league-phase match
value.hint: Kylian Mbappe scored four times; Chiquinho, Mehdi Taremi and Ayoub El Kaabi scored for Olympiacos.

archive.notes: Score, venue and scorers agree. Gulf News gives the day (Wednesday 26 November, a beIN URL also carries that date); beIN text is dated a day later in Australia.

value.name: Olympiacos won 1-0 at Kairat Almaty for their first Champions League win of the season
value.hint: Gelson Martins scored in the 73rd minute at the Astana Arena.

archive.notes: Date, score, scorer, minute and venue agree.

value.name: Olympiacos won 2-1 at Ajax in the final Champions League league-phase match
value.hint: Gelson Martins opened the scoring in the 52nd minute in Amsterdam.

archive.notes: Date, score and Martins 52nd minute agree; Hezze minute differs (79th vs 84th) so omitted.

value.name: Olympiacos named Imanol Alguacil as head coach
value.hint: He replaced Jose Luis Mendilibar and was introduced by president Evangelos Marinakis.

archive.notes: Date and appointment agree in both reports.

value.name: Jose Luis Mendilibar took charge of Olympiacos as head coach
value.hint: The Spanish coach arrived after winning the Europa League with Sevilla and later won the Conference League with the club.

archive.notes: Wikipedia states he is coach from 11 February; To Vima announces it that week. A transfer-news site dated 10 February says the club was set to announce him; the start date is taken from Wikipedia and To Vima.

value.name: Olympiacos beat OFI 4-2 in the Greek Cup final
value.hint: Lajos Detari scored twice, from a penalty and late in the match.

archive.notes: Single publisher (Wikipedia); second source not found. Owner 2026-10-09: approved on owner knowledge.

value.name: Olympiacos beat PAOK 2-0 in the second leg of the Greek Cup final
value.hint: Olympiacos won the two-leg final 3-1 on aggregate.

archive.notes: Single publisher (Wikipedia); RSSSF page returned 404. Owner 2026-10-09: approved on owner knowledge.

value.name: Olympiacos beat AEK Athens 3-0 in the last play-off match and celebrated their 45th league title
value.hint: Supporters gathered outside the stadium despite coronavirus restrictions.

archive.notes: Date corrected from 20 July to 19 July: Wikipedia ends the season on 19 July 2020 and Greek City Times (published Monday 20 July) places the fans outside the stadium on the Sunday, which is 19 July. Both give the 45th title; the 3-0 against AEK is from Greek City Times.

value.name: Olympiacos won 3-2 at Panionios to secure the league title
value.hint: The 37th league title came with three matches remaining.

archive.notes: Both UEFA reports are the same publisher; one gives 22 March, the other 23 March. Owner 2026-10-09: Wikipedia gives no match date, so only the year is stated.

value.name: Olympiacos were confirmed league champions even though they lost 2-1 at Larissa
value.hint: The title was settled when a rival lost, leaving Olympiacos eight points clear.

archive.notes: UEFA reports the Larissa match on 16 April; the Wikipedia season page shows a Larissa fixture on 3 April, so the date is unresolved. Owner 2026-10-09: Wikipedia gives no match date, so only the year is stated.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Iraklis 1-0 to reclaim the league title
value.hint: Rivaldo was on target as the club completed a domestic double.

archive.notes: Single publisher (UEFA). Owner 2026-10-09: approved on owner knowledge.

value.name: Olympiacos beat Bayer Leverkusen 2-0 in a Champions League league-phase match
value.hint: Costinha scored inside two minutes and Mehdi Taremi added a second before half-time.

archive.notes: beIN and UEFA agree on 20 January and 2-0; the UEFA league-phase listing (Tuesday 20 January 2026) and Wikipedia both name Olympiacos first, so the home venue is no longer in doubt.

value.name: Olympiacos lost 2-0 at home to Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League play-off first leg
value.hint: Patrik Schick scored twice in three minutes.

archive.notes: Single publisher (ESPN). Owner 2026-10-09: approved on owner knowledge.

value.name: Olympiacos was founded in Piraeus
value.hint: The club was officially recognised the following year.

archive.notes: Single publisher (Wikipedia). Owner 2026-10-09: Wikipedia is the tiebreak, so 16 May 1924 is the founding date.

value.name: Olympiacos drew 2-2 with AC Milan in their first European Cup match
value.hint: Konstantinos Papazoglou and Ilias Ifandis scored for Olympiacos, the first Greek club to play in European competition.

archive.notes: Wikipedia and RSSSF both give 13 September 1959 and a 2-2 first leg; RSSSF names Papazoglou and Ifandis. The earlier venue claim was not confirmed by RSSSF and is dropped.
